title: check_dissector_urls: use concurrent http requests
description:
Speed up the url checks by using multiple http requests in parallel.

Python's requests module supports only synchronous requests, use aiohttp
and asyncio instead.

Make link's validate method a coroutine that can be controlled by asyncio.
Run the checks in groups of 120 requests. This way, each group can use
cached results from previous groups. It would be possible to pass all
requests to aiohttp immediately. aiohttp would then run them based on its
internal connection limit (this defaults to 100). However, caching would
not work then. All requests would see an empty cache, this is checked
before a request is submitted to aiohttp.

The field name for the status code in aiohttp's response is "status". For
the requests module, it was called "status_code". Rename this everywhere.

Update the signal handler for the async operation. If we're interrupted
while we extract the urls from the source files, we can exit immediately.
If we're interrupted during the async link checking, we cancel all
requests from the current group and make sure that we're not starting
another group. When an async operation is cancelled, each coroutine and
the asyncio.gather() call receive an asyncio.CancelledError exception. We
have to handle these exceptions.

On my system, a complete run takes about 7 minutes now. We could speed
things up further by starting all tasks in parallel and using a different
approach for caching.

Please note that this change hasn't been tested on Windows. (Maybe the
sigint handling isn't portable anyway...)

notes.body: I needed to do 'pip install aiohttp' - not a problem.

This looks good to me.  I have not tried to test this script under Windows at all yet.

I did see this written to stdout or stderr (7 times):

"Can not load response cookies: Illegal key 'BIGipServerV19edYz/rGMxUCJeS7ZH3w'"

(I guess this can be ignored - the cookies may be malformed and can't be parsed - https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/issues/1842)

Running with --verbose, you can see a flurry of quick responses then sometimes a lengthy pause while the slowest responses come back.  This is definitely much faster than before (just under 8mins for me) - I wonder if using ThreadPoolExecutor would keep more attempts 'in flight' more of the time.  Does this task group approach mean that the results come back in a predictable order (rather than when they happen to complete) ?

Yes, that's certainly something to improve. The idea was to make cached results usable for requests in the next group (instead of fetching https://www.wireshark.org/tools/modelines.html 1000 times ;-).
My understanding of asyncio.gather() is that this waits until all tasks have returned, we can't make any assumptions about the order in which they're started or completed. As you say, if there's one url in the group where the server does not respond, we'll have to wait for the 25 sec timeout to expire.

ThreadPoolExecutor seems to be an alternative to asyncio, on which aiohttp is based. It looks like asyncio's TaskGroup mechanism would allow starting a number of tasks up front and for each task that is completed, we could kick off another one. I'll see if I can get this to work.
